metadata.question: Was the primary direction of the Eyjafjallajökull volcanic plume toward the north rather than the south on May 10, 2010?

data.raw_code: The user asks about the direction of the Eyjafjallajökull volcanic plume on May 10, 2010. To determine if it was primarily northward or southward, I need to: 1. Search strategy: - Use satellite imagery that can detect volcanic plumes (ash, SO2) - MODIS thermal anomalies (FIRMS) for fire/hotspots could show eruption activity - MODIS true color or aerosol products for visible plume - SO2 measurements from OMI or TROPOMI (but TROPOMI launched later) - Best option: MODIS true color to visually inspect plume direction 2. Geometry & Time: - Eyjafjallajökull volcano coordinates: approx 63.63°N, 19.62°W - Date: May 10, 2010 - Need imagery from that specific day 3. Approach: - Use MODIS Terra (MOD09GA) or Aqua (MYD09GA) surface reflectance for true color - Create a true color composite (bands 1,4,3) - Analyze plume extent by looking at visible ash/cloud patterns - Calculate plume centroid or directional distribution 4. Challenges: - May 2010 had significant eruption activity - Cloud cover might obscure plume - Need clear pass from MODIS on that day 5. Logic for direction determination: - Option 1: Calculate mean latitude of plume pixels (above certain reflectance threshold) - Option 2: Compare pixel counts north vs south of volcano - If mean plume latitude > volcano latitude (63.63°N) → plume northward - If mean plume latitude < volcano latitude → plume southward 6. Data Quality: - Check MODIS collection size for May 10, 2010 - If no MODIS, try Landsat 7 (ETM+ SLC-on) or Landsat 5 - After cloud masking, check valid pixel count - Validate that calculated latitude is reasonable (not NaN, within bounds) Let me structure the code: 1. Define volcano point and date 2. Get MODIS Terra imagery for May 10, 2010 3. If no data, try MODIS Aqua or Landsat 4. Create true color composite 5. Mask clouds using MODIS quality band 6. Identify plume pixels (high reflectance in visible bands) 7. Calculate mean latitude of plume pixels 8. Compare to volcano latitude 9. Output result with validation stats ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const volcano = ee.Geometry.Point(-19.62, 63.63); // Eyjafjallajökull const roi = volcano.buffer(50000); // 50km buffer around volcano // Specific date: May 10, 2010 const startDate = '2010-05-10'; const endDate = '2010-05-11'; // 2. Data Acquisition - Try MODIS Terra first let modisTerra = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/006/MOD09GA') .filterDate(startDate, endDate) .filterBounds(roi); let modisCount = modisTerra.size().getInfo(); console.log(`MODIS Terra images: ${modisCount}`); let collection = modisTerra; // Fallback to MODIS Aqua if Terra has no data if (modisCount === 0) { console.log('Trying MODIS Aqua...'); let modisAqua = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/006/MYD09GA') .filterDate(startDate, endDate) .filterBounds(roi); let aquaCount = modisAqua.size().getInfo(); console.log(`MODIS Aqua images: ${aquaCount}`); if (aquaCount === 0) { // Try Landsat 7 as last resort (SLC-on in 2010) console.log('Trying Landsat 7...'); let landsat = ee.ImageCollection('LANDSAT/LE07/C02/T1_L2') .filterDate(startDate, endDate) .filterBounds(roi); let landsatCount = landsat.size().getInfo(); console.log(`Landsat 7 images: ${landsatCount}`); if (landsatCount === 0) { console.log('C1'); return; } collection = landsat; } else { collection = modisAqua; } } // Get the first image let image = ee.Image(collection.first()); // 3. Processing - Create true color and mask clouds // For MODIS if (collection.getInfo().id.includes('MODIS')) { // MODIS true color: bands 1, 4, 3 (R,G,B) image = image.select(['sur_refl_b01', 'sur_refl_b04', 'sur_refl_b03']); // Simple cloud mask using MODIS quality band let qa = image.select('sur_refl_b01').gt(0); // Valid reflectance > 0 image = image.updateMask(qa); } // For Landsat else if (collection.getInfo().id.includes('LANDSAT')) { // Landsat true color: bands 3,2,1 image = image.select(['SR_B3', 'SR_B2', 'SR_B1']); // Apply scale factors image = image.multiply(0.0000275).add(-0.2); // Simple cloud mask using QA band let qa = image.select('SR_B1').gt(0); image = image.updateMask(qa); } // 4. Identify plume pixels (high reflectance in red band) let redBand = image.select(0); // First band is red let plumeMask = redBand.gt(0.3); // Threshold for bright plume // Create latitude image let latImage = ee.Image.pixelLonLat().select('latitude'); // Get mean latitude of plume pixels let stats = plumeMask.addBands(latImage).reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean().combine({ reducer2: ee.Reducer.count(), sharedInputs: true }), geometry: roi, scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9 }); let meanLat = stats.get('latitude_mean').getInfo(); let pixelCount = stats.get('latitude_count').getInfo(); console.log(`Plume pixel count: ${pixelCount}`); console.log(`Mean plume latitude: ${meanLat}`); console.log(`Volcano latitude: 63.63`); // 5. Validation & Final Answer if (pixelCount === 0) { console.log('C2'); return; } if (meanLat === null || meanLat === undefined || isNaN(meanLat) || meanLat < 50 || meanLat > 70) { console.log('C3'); return; } // Determine if plume is primarily northward // If mean plume latitude > volcano latitude + 0.1 degrees (~11 km north) if (meanLat > 63.73) { console.log('A'); } else if (meanLat < 63.53) { console.log('B'); } else { // Plume centered around volcano, ambiguous direction console.log('C3'); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
